title: Methods and limitations ledger
description: Per repository, each statistical or machine-learning method used, its assumptions and its known limitations, each tied to the file and verbatim sentence in the owning repository where it is stated. Nothing here is new analysis: it restates what the repositories already say about themselves. Checked by tools/check_ledger.py.

rows.method: Expert-coded crosswalk of performance-influencing factors across HFACS, IDHEAS-G, SPAR-H, CREAM and HSE, plus a rule engine that turns analyst-supplied factor levels into an ordinal screening band.

assumptions.text: Factor levels are supplied by an analyst; the engine cannot check them.
assumptions.quote: Factor levels are inputs.** The engine reasons from levels an analyst supplies and cannot check whether those levels are right.

assumptions.text: The screening bands rest on thresholds the author chose.
assumptions.quote: The screening bands rest on thresholds the author chose.

caveats.text: Same-coder limitation: every match strength is one person's judgement, with no second coder.
caveats.quote: Every match strength, every asserted absence and every PIF-to-function assignment is one person's judgement. No second coder reviewed them.

caveats.text: No inter-rater reliability statistic exists.
caveats.quote: Because there was one coder, there is no agreement statistic to report.

caveats.text: The output is an ordinal band, not a probability, and is not calibrated.
caveats.quote: It is not a human error probability, not a rate, and not calibrated against anything.

caveats.text: Factor-to-error-mode links are unvalidated propositions from the literature.
caveats.quote: No effect size is attached to any of them and none has been tested against outcome data.

caveats.text: Domain transfer from nuclear power and aviation is an extension the sources do not license.
caveats.quote: Using this vocabulary in chemical manufacturing is an extension, not an application.

caveats.text: CREAM conditions were transcribed at one remove, from Shirali et al. (2019).
caveats.quote: Hollnagel's book was not consulted; the nine CPCs come from Shirali et al. (2019).

rows.method: Transparent rule-based suggester (97 curated phrase rules, no ML) from incident text to candidate PIFs, scored by precision and recall against PIFs hand-coded for 23 CSB investigations in a development and a held-out cohort.

assumptions.text: Gold labels are the author's own codings; a PIF is coded only when a passage was quoted for it.
assumptions.quote: The gold labels are incomplete (a PIF is coded only when a passage was quoted for it), so a false positive may be a real condition nobody coded.

caveats.text: Same-coder limitation: the same person coded both cohorts and wrote the rules; no second-coder data exists yet.
caveats.quote: **Status: no second coder has contributed yet, so there are no agreement figures.**

caveats.text: The development-cohort scores are resubstitution and optimistic.
caveats.quote: the curated scores on it are resubstitution and optimistic

caveats.text: Held-out recall may be inflated by how passages were chosen.
caveats.quote: which inflates recall

caveats.text: Ten of the 20 PIFs have gold coding in either cohort; the rules for the other ten are untested.
caveats.quote: Ten of the 20 PIFs have gold coding in either cohort, so the rules for the other ten remain untested.

caveats.text: No confidence interval is claimed for the held-out results.
caveats.quote: no confidence interval is claimed

rows.method: Plausibility screen on Form 300A filings (hours per employee within 120 to 4,500, positive hours, at least one employee, non-negative counts) and the screened versus unscreened aggregate TRIR, DART, LTIR and severity rates (ratio of sums, per 200,000 hours).

assumptions.text: Each aggregate rate is a ratio of sums, not a mean of establishment rates.
assumptions.quote: Each aggregate is a ratio of sums (total numerator over total hours across filings), not a mean of establishment rates.

caveats.text: The screen is a threshold rule, not a ground-truth label of error.
caveats.quote: **The plausibility screen is a threshold rule**, not a ground-truth label for

caveats.text: The screen does not cover the day-count fields, so the severity rate stays exposed to mistyped day totals.
caveats.quote: It does not screen the day-count fields (K, L)

caveats.text: The flagged share depends on the chosen bounds and should be quoted with its range.
caveats.quote: is a property of the chosen bounds and should be quoted with the range.

caveats.text: The planned ITA versus BLS SOII comparison figure was not produced.
caveats.quote: was not produced.

caveats.text: Unscreened aggregates are not usable for an ITA versus SOII comparison in 2019 and 2024.
caveats.quote: Unscreened ITA aggregates are not usable for a SOII comparison in 2019 and 2024

caveats.text: Wilson intervals treat filings as independent, so they are narrower than clustered intervals.
caveats.quote: Wilson intervals treat filings as independent.

caveats.text: Reporting scope: only establishments filing with OSHA are covered.
caveats.quote: The dataset covers only establishments filing with OSHA

rows.method: Year-to-year persistence of flagged filings by establishment_id: transition matrix, odds ratio, Cohen's kappa and a permutation test (200 permutations) that holds each year's flag count fixed.

assumptions.text: Establishments are keyed on establishment_id throughout.
assumptions.quote: this analysis is keyed on `establishment_id` throughout

caveats.text: Association, not causation: the permutation test does not identify a mechanism.
caveats.quote: **Association, not causation.**

caveats.text: establishment_id tracks a site more than a fixed legal filer: 25.3% of IDs carry more than one EIN.
caveats.quote: 313,527 of 1,238,236 establishment IDs (25.3%) appear with more than one distinct EIN across years

caveats.text: The screen cannot separate repeated data-entry mistakes from a genuinely unusual, correctly reported hours profile.
caveats.quote: The panel result cannot distinguish

caveats.text: Coverage is uneven: only 1.3% of establishments appear in all 9 years.
caveats.quote: Only 1.3% of establishments appear in all 9 years

caveats.text: Kappa of 0.28 means most flagged filings are not matched by a flag in the adjacent year; both persistent and one-off causes likely coexist.
caveats.quote: This is a qualified result, not an absolute one

rows.method: Preregistered 2025 predictions: point value is the mean of the last three observed years, with a 95% interval from a back-test of the same rule (Student t, 6 degrees of freedom, times the RMS of six one-step errors), on a transformed scale.

assumptions.text: The stated 95% is nominal because it rests on only six back-test errors.
assumptions.quote: With six errors this is an approximation and the stated 95% is nominal.

assumptions.text: Scoring assumes the repository pipeline and plausibility screen are unchanged for 2025.
assumptions.quote: The 2025 values will also depend on whether the pipeline's inputs and plausibility screen are unchanged

caveats.text: Q3 (unscreened TRIR) and Q4 (flagged-hours share) have intervals close to uninformative because of extreme hours outliers in 2019 and 2024; Q1, Q2 and Q6.x are the informative tests.
caveats.quote: Q3 and Q4 have very wide intervals because the hours column contains extreme outliers in 2019 and 2024

caveats.text: The miss-count calibration reading assumes independence, which is not true here (size bands move together; Q1 and Q4 share filings).
caveats.quote: Independence is not true here

rows.method: Covariate-adjusted Poisson, negative binomial (NB2), zero-inflated Poisson and zero-inflated NB2 models of 2024 recordable cases with a log-hours offset, size-band and NAICS 4-digit fixed effects, compared by likelihood and AIC.

assumptions.text: The zero-inflation probability pi is a single constant per fit, a deliberate restriction for identification.
assumptions.quote: `pi` is a single constant per fit; the inflation equation carries no covariates.

caveats.text: No causal reading of the size-band and sub-industry coefficients.
caveats.quote: No causal reading.

caveats.text: Fits condition on passing the screen; excess zeros cannot be split between incident-free operation and under-recording.
caveats.quote: Excess zeros in particular cannot be split between genuinely incident-free operation and under-recording

caveats.text: Only the 30 largest NAICS-3 groups (at least 500 screened establishments) are fitted, so results describe large industries.
caveats.quote: so the 30-of-30 result is a statement about large industries, not about every industry.

caveats.text: Subsampling of the four largest groups affects absolute log-likelihoods and AIC differences there.
caveats.quote: Subsampling of the four largest groups affects absolute log-likelihoods

rows.method: Exact (Garwood) Poisson intervals for a TRIR and an exact conditional test and power calculation for comparing two rates, giving site-years needed per size band.

assumptions.text: Cases over a fixed exposure are modelled as Poisson.
assumptions.quote: Cases over a fixed exposure are modelled as Poisson

caveats.text: Poisson is a best case; real establishment counts are overdispersed, so real detectability is worse.
caveats.quote: Poisson is a best case.

caveats.text: Band means stand in for establishments and flatter small sites because hours are skewed.
caveats.quote: the mean-size result flatters small sites.

caveats.text: This is a planning calculation, not a test applied to any real pair of sites.
caveats.quote: This is a planning calculation, not a test applied to any real pair of sites.

rows.method: Deterministic lexical scorer: substring and prefix concept coverage over alternation lists, numeric-fact matching, and an assertion-versus-mention heuristic (70-character left contrast window) that yields the adjacent-substitution rate.

assumptions.text: Answer keys use alternation groups with several surface forms, and every reference answer must satisfy its own key.
assumptions.quote: answer keys use alternation groups with several surface forms

caveats.text: Measured accuracy is a lower bound on substantive correctness; paraphrased correct answers are scored as misses.
caveats.quote: Measured accuracy is therefore a **lower bound** on substantive correctness

caveats.text: The contrast heuristic is the weakest link and misfires in both directions.
caveats.quote: ## 2. The contrast heuristic is the weakest link

caveats.text: Any adjacent-substitution rate must be checked against a human-adjudicated subsample.
caveats.quote: any published adjacent-substitution rate must be checked against a human-adjudicated subsample

caveats.text: Citation grading is structural: it does not confirm the system retrieved or used the clause.
caveats.quote: It does not confirm that the system retrieved that clause, read it, or used it

caveats.text: Category-error items are poorly served by the abstention cue list (1 of 5 oracle answers trips it).
caveats.quote: only 1 of 5 trips the abstention detector

rows.method: McNemar's exact test on discordant items and percentile cluster bootstrap over item families (with Wilson intervals alongside) for paired, clustered accuracy comparisons.

assumptions.text: Every arm answers every item; the code refuses to compare arms with different item sets.
assumptions.quote: which raises if two arms' item sets differ

caveats.text: With 44 family clusters the intervals are wide; a null result means the corpus cannot resolve a difference of that size, not equivalence.
caveats.quote: A null result should be read as "this corpus cannot resolve a difference of this size," not as "the arms are equivalent."

caveats.text: The corpus is a hand-built construct by one author with no sampling frame, so error rates cannot be generalised.
caveats.quote: there is no sampling frame and no basis for generalising

caveats.text: Single-author and unreviewed: no external review of the answer keys.
caveats.quote: There has been no external review of the answer keys.

caveats.text: Contamination of open-web regulation text is unmeasured.
caveats.quote: This has not been probed.

rows.method: Selective prediction: tie-aware risk-coverage curves, AURC and E-AURC, and selective accuracy at 25, 50 and 75 percent coverage, with cluster-bootstrap intervals, on the 63 factual items.

assumptions.text: A retriever's confidence is its top retrieval score, a similarity and not a probability.
assumptions.quote: which is a similarity, not a probability

caveats.text: AURC intervals (for example TF-IDF) include the uninformative value, so the retrieval score is only a weak abstention signal.
caveats.quote: the AURC intervals (for example TF-IDF [0.385, 0.751]) include the uninformative

caveats.text: Fused-rank scores take few distinct values, so most items tie and carry almost no signal.
caveats.quote: Reciprocal rank fusion scores take few distinct values, so most items tie

caveats.text: No language model was run, so none of these numbers describe any language model.
caveats.quote: The numbers say nothing about any language model: none was run.

rows.method: Calibration of a confidence score: Brier score against the base-rate reference, ten-bin equal-width expected calibration error and a reliability table, with cluster-bootstrap intervals.

assumptions.text: The metrics treat the confidence as a probability, so values outside [0, 1] are rejected, not rescaled.
assumptions.quote: the code rejects values outside [0, 1] instead of rescaling them

caveats.text: Calibration is computable only for TF-IDF: BM25, BM25+ and RRF scores are not probability-scale, and random_floor and oracle report no confidence.
caveats.quote: Brier and ECE are therefore not computed for BM25, BM25+ or RRF

caveats.text: ECE is biased upward on small samples and is a coarse summary here (6 of 10 bins occupied).
caveats.quote: ECE depends on the bin count and is biased upward on small samples

caveats.text: TF-IDF's reliability bins are sparse and the curve is not monotone.
caveats.quote: **The bins are sparse.**

rows.method: Source verification of 68 corpus items against a dated eCFR edition (section resolves, verbatim anchor present, paragraph markers present, anchor inside the cited paragraph), with unverifiable drafts quarantined and excluded from scoring.

assumptions.text: Quarantined drafts are excluded by construction: the loader never reads the quarantine file.
assumptions.quote: the loader never reads that file

assumptions.text: Federal regulation (29, 40 and 46 CFR) is used as a proxy for copyrighted consensus standards.
assumptions.quote: ## 3. Federal regulation is a proxy for consensus standards

caveats.text: Quarantined items: six drafted items (NFPA 70E, API 520, API 754, ISO 4126) could not be verified and are excluded.
caveats.quote: holds six drafted items that could not be verified

caveats.text: Four further regulatory-currency drafts are quarantined until current eCFR text is confirmed.
caveats.quote: A further four regulatory-currency drafts

caveats.text: Verification checks provenance, not editorial quality; an audit found a defect (fe-002) that 68/68 passing did not expose.
caveats.quote: The verification passing is weaker evidence than it looks

caveats.text: The verification report is pinned to one eCFR edition and cannot detect later regulatory change.
caveats.quote: it cannot detect that a regulation changed after the report was written.

caveats.text: Utility weights and risk tiers are stated policy judgements, not measurements.
caveats.quote: are stated judgements, not measured or elicited quantities.

rows.method: Peer-group TRIR and DART benchmarks from OSHA Injury Tracking Application establishment records (CY2023-CY2025), compared within industry peer groups.

assumptions.text: Comparisons are made within a peer group, never against the site-wide total.
assumptions.quote: Compare within a peer group, never against the site-wide total.

caveats.text: ITA is not a random sample; its aggregate rate runs above the BLS national figure.
caveats.quote: **ITA is not a random sample.**

caveats.text: Everything is self-reported and unaudited; under-recording is a known, unmeasured problem.
caveats.quote: Under-recording is a known, unmeasured problem.

caveats.text: The plausibility test catches unit errors, not scope errors.
caveats.quote: **The plausibility test catches unit errors, not scope errors.**

caveats.text: Year-over-year is not a fixed panel; trends conflate real change with who reported.
caveats.quote: Sector trends conflate real change with changes in who reported

caveats.text: OIICS codes are model-predicted by OSHA, not human-assigned.
caveats.quote: **OIICS codes are model-predicted by OSHA**

caveats.text: Single-establishment rates are noisy.
caveats.quote: **Single-establishment rates are noisy.**

rows.method: Empirical-Bayes Gamma-Poisson shrinkage of small-establishment rates toward a 2-digit NAICS peer rate (method-of-moments prior), alongside exact Garwood intervals.

assumptions.text: Establishment true rates are Gamma-distributed within a peer group and cases are Poisson.
assumptions.quote: Each establishment has a true rate lambda drawn from a peer-group Gamma

assumptions.text: The credible interval is only as good as the Gamma-Poisson assumption and the peer-group definition.
assumptions.quote: It is only as good as the Gamma-Poisson assumption and the peer-group definition

caveats.text: The fitted dispersion absorbs reporting error, so it is an upper-side estimate of true rate heterogeneity.
caveats.quote: it is an upper-side estimate of true rate heterogeneity

caveats.text: The method-of-moments estimate treats mu as known, so it is slightly biased in small groups; only sectors with at least 300 establishments are fitted.
caveats.quote: so it is slightly biased in small groups

caveats.text: For any single establishment shrinkage can move the estimate away from the truth.
caveats.quote: for any single establishment it can move the estimate away from the truth

caveats.text: The committed fit uses single-establishment records for 2024 only.
caveats.quote: The committed fit uses single-establishment records only

rows.method: Address-based linkage of EPA RMP facilities to OSHA Form 300A and Severe Injury Reports, descriptive group comparisons, within-band Spearman rank stability and an exact-Poisson funnel-style peer band.

assumptions.text: RMP release coverage assumes continuous observation between the first submission (less five years) and the last.
assumptions.quote: our observation window assumes continuous coverage between the first submission

caveats.text: Join error: no shared identifier; only 48.83% of RMP plants join to an injury filing, and joined plants are not a random sample.
caveats.quote: Only 48.83% of RMP plants join to an injury filing

caveats.text: Confounding: one-way breakdowns with no adjustment.
caveats.quote: No adjustment is made.

caveats.text: No hypothesis tests or confidence intervals are reported for group comparisons; small cells rest on a few dozen events.
caveats.quote: We report counts rather than tests

caveats.text: Release history is partly mechanical and may reflect reporting behaviour.
caveats.quote: may reflect reporting behaviour rather than underlying hazard

caveats.text: All three sources are self-reported by employers.
caveats.quote: All three sources are filed by employers.

caveats.text: Not suitable for enforcement or for ranking plants for public blame.
caveats.quote: it is not suitable for enforcement or for ranking plants for public blame

rows.method: Four-line cost-benefit model (annual benefit, residual cost, payback, ROI) with tornado sensitivity, breakeven views and seeded uniform Monte Carlo over assumed input ranges.

assumptions.text: Input ranges are assumptions: the default 30% half-width is a placeholder, not a finding.
assumptions.quote: The 30% is a placeholder, not a finding.

assumptions.text: Uniform sampling treats all values in a range as equally plausible and independent.
assumptions.quote: Uniform sampling treats all values in a range as equally plausible and independent

caveats.text: ROI is cumulative benefit over investment, not net return.
caveats.quote: **ROI here is cumulative benefit over investment, not net return.**

caveats.text: Risk reduction is an input the user supplies; it is the largest weakness of the model.
caveats.quote: **Risk reduction is an input you supply, not something the tool knows.**

caveats.text: Nothing is discounted, so long-horizon ROI is overstated; there is no NPV or IRR.
caveats.quote: **Nothing is discounted.**

caveats.text: Benefits are assumed flat and permanent over the horizon.
caveats.quote: **Benefits are assumed flat and permanent.**

caveats.text: Adding cost lines can never weaken the case, by construction.
caveats.quote: **Counting more cost can never weaken the case, by construction.**

caveats.text: Monte Carlo propagates uncertainty but does not reduce it.
caveats.quote: **Monte Carlo propagates uncertainty; it does not reduce it.**

rows.method: NWS heat index (Steadman simple formula then Rothfusz regression with low- and high-humidity adjustments) checked against the heat-index triggers of OSHA's proposed heat rule.

assumptions.text: NWS values assume shade.
assumptions.quote: NWS values assume shade;

caveats.text: WBGT omitted: the alternative WBGT triggers are not implemented because no numeric WBGT value was verified.
caveats.quote: the alternative WBGT triggers (NIOSH alert and exposure limits) are not, because no numeric WBGT value was verified.

caveats.text: The triggers come from a proposed rule that is not in force.
caveats.quote: this is a proposed rule, not in force.

caveats.text: Full sun can add up to 15 F to NWS values; not legal or medical advice.
caveats.quote: full sun can add up to 15 F.

rows.method: Two-step limited-information structural equation model estimator in numpy (measurement model, then structural model) with analytic and percentile-bootstrap standard errors.

assumptions.text: Indicators are continuous and multivariate normal.
assumptions.quote: Indicators are continuous and multivariate normal.

assumptions.text: Only recursive models with congeneric measurement blocks are supported.
assumptions.quote: **Only recursive models with congeneric measurement blocks** are supported.

caveats.text: The estimator is limited-information, not full-information ML, so chi-square values differ from lavaan or Mplus.
caveats.quote: **The estimator is limited-information, not ML.**

caveats.text: Analytic standard errors are too narrow; the bootstrap is the supported path.
caveats.quote: **Analytic standard errors are known to be too narrow**

caveats.text: Ordinal indicators are treated as continuous; a polychoric approach is not implemented.
caveats.quote: **Ordinal indicators are treated as continuous.**

caveats.text: Missing data are handled by listwise deletion only.
caveats.quote: no missing-data handling beyond listwise deletion

caveats.text: No empirical validation: nothing has been fitted to real injury data.
caveats.quote: **No empirical validation.**

rows.method: Monte Carlo simulation studies of sample-size requirements (fit-test power, path precision, ranking of paths) for a five-latent, three-indicator model, and of standard-error coverage.

assumptions.text: Results are simulation under the stated model (identical loadings, normal errors).
assumptions.quote: Limits: simulation under the model you state

caveats.text: Simulation only: no real injury, incident or survey data were analysed.
caveats.quote: Simulation only. No real injury, incident or survey data were analysed

caveats.text: One structural model and one set of measurement conditions in Study 1.
caveats.quote: One structural model and one set of measurement conditions in Study 1.

caveats.text: The bootstrap comparison rests on 40 replications.
caveats.quote: The bootstrap comparison rests on 40 replications.

caveats.text: Study 1 did not record fit indices per replication.
caveats.quote: Study 1 did not record fit indices per replication
